name: CsNO3 phase II, 296 K
citation: D. Pohl and T. Gross (1993). Caesium nitrate (II) at 296 K. Acta Crystallographica Section C 49, 316-318.
measurement_conditions_evidence: Temperature verified from original publisher first page, not inferred from synthesis or a nominal ambient value. No numerical pressure verified.
method: Experimental single-crystal X-ray diffraction on Enraf-Nonius CAD-4 using graphite-monochromated Ag K-alpha radiation0.56087A. Original publisher page316 reports a=10.902(2), c=7.740(2) A and R=.019, wR=.027, agreeing with the deposited geometry.
synthesis_conditions: Single crystals grown by slow evaporation of aqueous solution at292K, as described on original page316. Growth temperature is separate from296K diffraction.
notes: All three inequivalent Cs sites are retained with multiplicity3 and population1/3 each.
The raw deposited CIF omits atomic occupancies; a full-occupancy ordered structure is its parser/default crystallographic interpretation, not an independently refined occupancy measurement.

The original article abstract reports F(000)=774 and absorption coefficient102.04cm^-1; raw COD fields read765 and5.44mm^-1. These non-geometric metadata discrepancies are retained and disclosed; no coordinate or unit-cell correction is applied.
All cell parameters and coordinates are from this exact deposited experimental CIF. No species replacement, generic ideal model, coordinate substitution or cell rescaling.
K edge selected for broad EXAFS reference coverage. A computed FEFF k grid does not establish the usable experimental k range.
Native degeneracy is per absorber. An ensemble of inequivalent sites requires explicit normalized site weights; do not sum all sites at full amplitude.

This reference retains a selected nearest-12 oxygen envelope at each inequivalent Cs site, not a uniquely established chemical coordination shell. The accessible primary article does not assign CN12 explicitly; all actual distances and excluded neighbors are preserved in provenance.

The 3.95 A selection cutoff is an explicit common envelope boundary. The per-site gaps from the twelfth to thirteenth O neighbor are 0.137535, 0.462309 and 0.264545 A for Cs sites 1, 2 and 3 respectively; longer included contacts must not be treated as equivalent bonds.

For Cs site 3, the thirteenth O neighbor at 3.972503 A lies inside the native RPATH=4 A calculation radius but is deliberately not selected in the nearest-12 envelope. A shell-limited database selection is distinct from every path generated within RPATH.
All three inequivalent Cs sites have population weight 1/3. Native degeneracy is per absorber: an ensemble model needs explicit normalized site weights, not all three sites summed at full amplitude.
